title: US troop withdrawal leaves Kurds at mercy of Iran & Baghdad, says former State Department official Victoria Taylor
gist: Al-Monitor's 'On the Middle East with Amberin Zaman' features Victoria Taylor, former deputy assistant secretary of state for Iraq and Iran affairs, arguing that the withdrawal of the last US troops from Erbil ends the era in which the Kurds were America's closest ally in Iraq and leaves them exposed to Iran and Baghdad.

themes.theme: End of the US-Kurdish era in Iraq

insights.claim: The withdrawal of the last US troops from Erbil marks the end of the era in which the Kurds were the United States' closest ally in Iraq, according to former deputy assistant secretary of state Victoria Taylor.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A named former Iraq/Iran policy principal calling it an era's end signals a durable US posture change in northern Iraq, not a tactical redeployment.
insights.quote: The withdrawal of the last US troops from Erbil marks the end of an era in which the Kurds were the United States' closest ally in Iraq
insights.locator: The withdrawal of the last US troops from Erbil

insights.claim: With US forces gone from Erbil, the Kurds are left at the mercy of Iran and Baghdad, according to the framing of Taylor's argument in this episode.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Kurdistan Region autonomy and its oil-export leverage against Baghdad are the assets most directly repriced by a US exit.
insights.quote: US troop withdrawal leaves Kurds at mercy of Iran & Baghdad
insights.locator: US troop withdrawal leaves Kurds at mercy of Iran & Baghdad

insights.claim: The assessment carries weight because it comes from the former US deputy assistant secretary of state responsible for Iraq and Iran affairs, not an outside commentator.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Ex-officials with the Iraq/Iran portfolio are the best available read on internal US thinking once policy has already shifted.
insights.quote: Victoria Taylor, former deputy assistant secretary of state for Iraq and Iran affairs
insights.locator: says Victoria Taylor, former deputy assistant secretary

insights.claim: Al-Monitor is routing this analysis through Amberin Zaman's interview programme, indicating the Kurdish-exposure question is being treated as a headline regional story rather than a niche one.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Editorial prioritisation is a weak but real signal that the Erbil withdrawal is becoming a mainstream regional risk theme.
insights.locator: On the Middle East with Amberin Zaman
